descriptor: Transformer bushing maker localising resin-impregnated (RIP) cores
lede: A Vadodara maker of transformer bushings, the insulated connectors that carry current in and out of every transformer, selling to OEMs and utilities in 60+ countries. Revenue grew 57% in FY26 with a 25.7% EBITDA margin, and management guides 40-45% growth in FY27 as a new plant starts making the RIP cores it now imports. The stock prices in a great deal of that: ~87x earnings and ~60x EBITDA.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue ₹235 Cr (+57%), EBITDA ₹60 Cr (25.7% margin), PAT ₹37 Cr; order book ₹400 Cr+. FY27 guidance: 40-45% growth (the CMD also said ₹360-400 Cr of invoicing) at a 24-25% EBITDA margin, with margins rising from FY28 once the Jarod plant makes RIP cores.

The Jarod plant slipped from 'ready by March 2026' to trial production by September and commercial output from October. Profit outruns cash (₹90 Cr of profit vs ₹49 Cr of operating cash flow over FY22-26) and inventory days hit 201. A ₹100-110 Cr equity raise is planned, and a ₹2.1 Cr cyber fraud hit FY26.
~87x trailing earnings against Quality Power at 81x, TARIL at 32x and Shilchar at 31x.

blocks.text: Yash makes oil-impregnated (OIP) and resin-impregnated (RIP) bushings up to 245 kV and high-current bushings, and offers retrofit services. RIP bushings are built on capacitive cores it now imports from a European technology partner; the new Jarod plant near Vadodara will make those cores in-house up to 550 kV, which also lifts the partner's restriction on exporting RIP bushings.

blocks.text: Management gives clear numbers and has met its revenue and margin promises so far; the plant timeline has slipped by about six months. The two FY27 revenue figures from the same call (40-45% growth and ₹360-400 Cr) don't reconcile.

items.text: Promoters held 57.9% at Mar 2026 and 53.8% at Sep 2026; we have not checked the reason for the fall.
Foreign institutions rose to 2.3%; domestic institutions 9.7%; shareholders up from ~2,500 to ~6,400 in a year.
A ₹2.10 Cr cyber fraud by a third party was found in FY26; legal action is under way.
The CMD's pay rose 107% to 53 times the median employee.
Auditors reported no key audit matters; the emphasis of matter only covers the first-time move to Ind AS.
Sukrut Electric is 50% owned jointly with Quality Power, also a listed peer.

blocks.note: No listed pure-play bushing maker; these are listed transformer and grid-equipment peers. In India, CG Power, Hitachi India and MIM are also building local RIP capacity (May 2026 call p.20).

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

Yash has delivered on growth and margins, and localising RIP cores could lift both further. But even our bull case barely beats today's price; the stock needs the plant to work on time and growth to stay above 40% for several years. The H1 FY27 results (21 Oct) and the Jarod start are the next tests.
